subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Endocrine therapy in breast cancer: classes, mechanisms and safety

steps.tx: Selective receptor modulation provides targeted antagonism in breast tissues while exerting distinct secondary effects. **Tamoxifen** is a selective **oestrogen receptor modulator** SERM competitively inhibiting oestrogen binding in breast tissue while acting as an agonist in endometrium and bone. In premenopausal hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer, 5 to 10 years of adjuvant tamoxifen significantly reduces recurrence and contralateral breast malignancy, though increasing risk of endometrial hyperplasia and thromboembolism.
steps.say: Selective receptor modulation provides targeted antagonism in breast tissues while exerting distinct secondary effects. Tamoxifen is a selective oestrogen receptor modulator SERM competitively inhibiting oestrogen binding in breast tissue while acting as an agonist in endometrium and bone. In premenopausal hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, adjuvant tamoxifen significantly reduces recurrence, though increasing risk of thromboembolism.

left.title: Tamoxifen Antagonist Profile
points: Arrests cell cycle at G1 restriction point
Standard adjuvant therapy for premenopausal women

right.title: Tamoxifen Agonist Profile
points: Preserves bone mineral density in postmenopausal women
Elevates deep venous thrombosis and PE risk

steps.tx: Suppression of peripheral oestrogen biosynthesis forms the cornerstone of postmenopausal endocrine management. **Aromatase inhibitors** **anastrozole**, **letrozole**, and **exemestane** block the peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogens, requiring postmenopausal status or concurrent **ovarian suppression** with GnRH agonists to prevent reflex pituitary gonadotropin elevation. Proven superior to tamoxifen in postmenopausal early breast cancer, aromatase inhibitors accelerate bone mineral density loss and induce arthralgias.
steps.say: Suppression of peripheral oestrogen biosynthesis forms the cornerstone of postmenopausal endocrine management. Aromatase inhibitors anastrozole, letrozole, and exemestane block the peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogens, requiring postmenopausal status or concurrent ovarian suppression with GnRH agonists. steps.tx: Selective down-regulation accomplishes pure oestrogen antagonism devoid of agonistic tissue effects. **Fulvestrant** is a pure selective oestrogen receptor down-regulator SERD binding ER-alpha with high affinity, impairing receptor dimerization, and triggering rapid proteasomal **receptor degradation**. Administered as monthly intramuscular injections, fulvestrant lacks any endometrial agonist activity, providing an effective backbone for second-line endocrine therapy in metastatic breast cancer.

rows: Competitive ER antagonist in breast, agonist in uterus
Binds ER-alpha, blocks dimerization, induces proteasome breakdown
Pure antagonist: approved for ESR1-mutated tumours
Reversible competitive inhibitor of aromatase CYP19A1

steps.tx: Acquired endocrine resistance frequently emerges through ligand-independent conformational mutations in the receptor gene. **Elacestrant** is an oral SERD approved for metastatic ER-positive breast cancer harbouring activating **ESR1 mutations** following progression on prior endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors. In the randomized EMERALD phase 3 trial, elacestrant significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared to standard of care endocrine monotherapy in patients with detectable ESR1-mutant circulating tumour DNA.

nodes.label: Oral SERD Elacestrant Binds & Degrades ER

steps.tx: Cell cycle kinase inhibition synergizes with endocrine backbones to overcome hormone resistance. Adding **CDK4/6 inhibitors** **palbociclib**, **ribociclib**, or **abemaciclib** to aromatase inhibitors or fulvestrant significantly improves progression-free and overall survival in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. In randomized phase 3 trials, adding CDK4/6 inhibition doubled median progression-free survival compared to endocrine therapy alone, with neutropenia and diarrhoea being manageable class toxicities.

steps.tx: Suppression of pituitary gonadotropin secretion induces castrate sex steroid levels. **GnRH agonists** **goserelin** and **leuprolide** produce an initial flare of luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone before down-regulating GnRH receptors, achieving **medical castration** in prostate and premenopausal breast cancers. During initial administration in advanced prostate cancer, co-administration of an antiandrogen for 2 to 4 weeks is mandatory to prevent symptomatic disease flare from testosterone surge.
steps.say: Suppression of pituitary gonadotropin secretion induces castrate sex steroid levels. GnRH agonists goserelin and leuprolide produce an initial flare of luteinizing hormone before down-regulating receptors, achieving medical castration in prostate and premenopausal breast cancers. steps.tx: Direct competitive blockade of pituitary receptors bypasses initial gonadotropin surges. **GnRH antagonists** **degarelix** and oral **relugolix** competitively block pituitary GnRH receptors, producing rapid **testosterone suppression** without an initial surge or clinical disease flare. In phase 3 trials in advanced prostate adenocarcinoma, oral relugolix demonstrated sustained castration rates exceeding 96% alongside a 54% lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared to leuprolide.

left.title: GnRH Agonists (Leuprolide)
points: Monthly or depot subcutaneous / IM injections

right.title: GnRH Antagonists (Relugolix)
points: Rapid testosterone suppression (< 50 ng/dL by Day 4)
Lower incidence of major adverse cardiac events

steps.tx: Next-generation androgen receptor axis inhibitors suppress castration-resistant prostate cancer through complementary mechanisms. **Abiraterone acetate** irreversibly inhibits CYP17A1 17-alpha-hydroxylase and C17,20-lyase in adrenal and testicular tissues, requiring concurrent prednisone to prevent **mineralocorticoid excess** hypertension and hypokalaemia. In parallel, second-generation **androgen receptor inhibitors** **enzalutamide**, **apalutamide**, and **darolutamide** directly block androgen binding, nuclear translocation, and co-activator recruitment, prolonging overall survival across metastatic and non-metastatic disease.
